what_it_is_in_the_app: Google states the Mobile Ads SDK estimates general location from the IP address. The app itself never requests a location permission and holds no location data. Re-check developers.google.com/admob/android/privacy/play-data-disclosure at submission.
Never collected — no location permission is declared.
Display names are declared as user-generated content, not legal names.
UserDoc.email — password sign-up, Google/Discord OAuth, Apple relay address. Guest accounts have none, which is what makes this optional.

what_it_is_in_the_app: UserDoc._id, displayName, OAuth subject ids (oauth.google/discord/apple), userDevices keyed to userId.

UserDoc.lastLoginIp — the client IP of the most recent successful sign-in, kept for abuse and security. Play has no IP data type; this is the honest home and keeps the declaration in lockstep with Apple's Other Data row.
No in-app purchases anywhere in the dependency tree.
In-game chat — free text plus preset ids — persisted on the game record. Lobby chat is preset-capped and never outlives the room. Optional because a player need never send one.
No image picker; avatars are a URL carried over from the OAuth provider, never an uploaded file.

what_it_is_in_the_app: AdMob ad impressions/clicks, plus Sentry's react-navigation screen transitions. This is the row the AdMob SDK drives — hence shared.

what_it_is_in_the_app: Display names, authored custom maps, and abuse-report free text (max 1000 chars, moderation.schemas.ts).
Gameplay: finished-game records (seats, scores, deterministic action logs), leaderboard and rating rows, tutorial completion, seen feature intros.
Sentry (DSN-gated — a build with no DSN never initialises the SDK) plus the Mobile Ads SDK's own crash logs. Scrubbed through @trm/shared telemetry.ts before egress.
Sentry tracing spans, breadcrumbs and tags; the local crashCapture record a user can share from Settings -> About. Same scrubber.
Play Vitals is Google's own collection and needs no declaration here.
